transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Solutions), Sara Miller (Meridian Procurement), Tom Rivera (Meridian InfoSec), Jules Park (Meridian Platform), Karen O'Neill (Meridian Legal)

Summary (auto): kickoff for pilot and procurement pathway; discussed MSA/DPA redlines, KMS keying options, SLA targets, pilot commit window and pricing guardrails. Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining — big agenda today is to make sure we have a clear path for the pilot commit and line up the legal and security bits so procurement can move it through.  uh quick roll call?
[00:12] Sara (Meridian): sara here, procurement.
[00:14] Tom (Meridian): tom, infosec.
[00:16] Jules (Meridian): jules, platform.
[00:18] Karen (Meridian): karen, legal.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): priya from solutions, hi.
[00:22] Marcus (Redwood): marcus here.
[00:25] Alex (Redwood): cool thanks. so first, sara, what's your timeline — i'd like to see where procurement needs to land to start the PO.
[00:33] Sara (Meridian): yeah we are hoping to have a PO by october 6, that's the target transport window. but we need the msadpa redlines and the sla language cleared ideally this week to get our approval committee to ok. otherwise it slips.
[00:45] Alex (Redwood): ok, understood. we'll prioritize redlines. priya, quick note on the SLA — from our side what is realistic for pilot latency / uptime SLO?
[00:55] Priya (Redwood): for pilot traffic, if you run hosted api, we can commit to 99.5% availability and p95 latencies in the 120-250ms ballpark depending on model choice and sequence length. if you're pinning a dedicated pool, we can go to 99.9% and lower tail latencies but that requires reserved capacity commitment and pricing sync.
[01:18] Jules (Meridian): can you clarify what you mean by "hosted" — are you saying single-tenant? we need to understand isolation and keying.
[01:26] Priya (Redwood): yeah sorry — hosted means our standard multi-tenant public API. isolation is logical; for stronger controls we have dedicated pools and the private deployment that runs in your vpc/on-prem. KMS options: you can use Redwood-managed KMS or bring-your-own KMS (we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM integrations).
[01:44] Tom (Meridian): bw — about the brough-your-own KMS: for pci scope we need customer controlled keys, we need to know if you hold any key material or if the keystores ever touch redwood managed HSMs.
[01:56] Marcus (Redwood): good question. for BYOK we do a key wrap model where your master key lives in your KMS, we store only wrapped keys and we can restrict unwrap operations to your account and region; the key material is never exported to Redwood. there are caveats when you want cross-region failover, we can discuss.
[02:16] Karen (Meridian): legal will want explicit language in the dpa about key custody and key destruction on termination. also audit logging for key ops.
[02:25] Alex (Redwood): noted, karen. we'll provide suggested text. we'll add an appendix about key custody and purge procedures.
[02:33] Sara (Meridian): on pricing — procurement asks for a committed volume discount for the pilot if we hit 10M tokens per month. what's the delta between hosted list price and pilot committed pricing?
[02:45] Alex (Redwood): for a short pilot we typically offer a pilot discount vs list — somewhere between 20–30% depending on term and whether you take dedicated capacity. if you commit to 10M tokens and a three-month pilot we can structure a blended rate and cap overage.
[02:59] Sara (Meridian): can you put that in writing — we need a simple rate card for the PO.
[03:05] Alex (Redwood): yes we'll send a pilot SOW + rate card.
[03:09] [03:09] Priya (Redwood): small thing on cost vs latency: you can trade to cheaper quantized variants which reduce cost but increase latency slightly; you'll want to pick models and quantization that match your acceptance criteria. we can recommend defaults after we see sample payloads.
[03:30] Jules (Meridian): sample payloads — we'll share two production-ish prompt batches — about 75% short chat-type prompts and 25% long-form invoices.
[03:40] Priya (Redwood): perfect, that will help us recommend kernels, batching, and whether prefix cache is useful.
[03:48] [04:00] Tom (Meridian): security review — what logs do you expose? specifically request-level logs, api keys usage, and audit trails. we need retention controls.
[04:09] Marcus (Redwood): we expose request-level metadata (no PII unless you send it) with trace ids; full request payload logging is optional and we recommend customers enable it only in staging. retention is configurable; default 90 days for audit logs, 365 for billing events, but we can adjust via the console for enterprise plans.
[04:30] Tom (Meridian): ok and SOC 2 reports? do you have an authority to disclose?
[04:36] Alex (Redwood): yes we've got SOC 2 type 2 — we'll share the attestation under an NDA link.
[04:43] Karen (Meridian): legal question on indemnity — the msadpa in our template requires certain IP indemnities. are you able to accept standard vendor language?
[04:52] Alex (Redwood): we have some carve-outs we typically ask for. we can share redlines; let's align offline. we usually accept customer IP claims for content generated by the model but have carve-outs around third-party open weights and base model provider terms.
[05:10] Karen (Meridian): that is potentially ok but we'll need to see the exact wording.
[05:14] [05:20] Sara (Meridian): timeline risk: if legal and infosec need to review the msadpa then procurement won't sign until both sign off; what's the minimal package to unblock procurement approval?
[05:30] Alex (Redwood): minimal package: 1) MSA/DPA redline with highlighted key clauses 2) pilot SOW and rate card 3) SOC2 + security packet + KMS integration doc 4) basic runbook and SLA table. if we deliver those in the next four business days, is that enough to get you to your committee?
[05:50] Sara (Meridian): yes — if we have those docs by sept 22 the committee can review and on sept 24 we have an internal approval gate.
[05:58] Alex (Redwood): ok we'll aim for sept 22.
[06:02] Priya (Redwood): switching to technical — jules, can you share how you want to route traffic? do you want to do a small beta behind feature flag to 5% or go all-in?
[06:12] Jules (Meridian): we'll start small: 5–10% routing to the pilot endpoints, then expand over two weeks. we'll need a rollback plan and throttles.
[06:21] Priya (Redwood): got it. we'll provide recommended rollout steps and a circuit-breaker policy. we also recommend a canary with mirrored traffic for the first day.
[06:30] [06:40] Jules (Meridian): latency budget — we need 95th percentile under 250ms for chat UX. if we go hosted and use the larger model, is that feasible?
[06:48] Priya (Redwood): yes for shorter sequences it's feasible. invoices and long docs will bump latency; we can run batching and kv cache for repeated prefixes to cut cost and tail latency. for the 95th we should test with your invoices sample.
[07:02] Alex (Redwood): priya will run an initial perf sweep and share numbers.
[07:06] Priya (Redwood): i'll do that, but note that perf on long sequences with quantized models sometimes shows higher variance — we'll include both mean and tail metrics.
[07:18] [07:30] Tom (Meridian): about data residency — some of our customers restrict data to eu regions. does redwood support regional routing?
[07:37] Marcus (Redwood): yes regional routing and model pinning by region is supported. we can set policies so eu traffic never leaves eu for inference, and logs can be stored in region-specific buckets.
[07:48] Tom (Meridian): do you have attestations around data residency compliance?
[07:52] Alex (Redwood): we can share our data residency doc and a regional deployment map.
[07:58] [08:05] Karen (Meridian): one more legal — termination clause duration for the pilot, we want a 30-day termination with data purge. is that standard?
[08:12] Alex (Redwood): pilot SOW normally has 30-day notice for the pilot termination and we follow data purge within 30 days unless you request expedited deletion. we'll add data disposition language.
[08:23] Sara (Meridian): on billing, let's be explicit: we need visibility into tokenization, how you count embeddings vs generation, how rounding is done, and the billing cycle.
[08:36] Marcus (Redwood): billing breakdown is token-level; embeddings are billed per vector unit, generation per token; we'll provide a sample invoice and tokenization notes. for pilot we can do weekly reporting to help with cost forecasting.
[08:50] [09:00] Jules (Meridian): technical question: does the kv cache persist between requests for the same session? and how do you handle state?
[09:08] Priya (Redwood): kv cache persists per session in memory in the serving runtime; we also support a prefix cache for repeated prompts which is persisted on SSD and can survive node restarts depending on deployment type. for private deployments we can configure longer-lived cache.
[09:26] Alex (Redwood): a quick note — some of our automated language in the dpa refers to "model providers" and third-party model terms, legal may want to see a clarifying note about your responsibilities.
[09:37] Karen (Meridian): yes please.
[09:40] [10:00] Sara (Meridian): are there any limits on retraining or derivative model claims? we need to ensure customer data can't be used to train public models.
[10:09] Alex (Redwood): we have an explicit clause: we don't use customer data for training unless agreed; for hosted customers we provide an opt-out and for private there is no training leakage. we'll include that in the dpa language.
[10:22] Tom (Meridian): what's your incident response time? we need an incident SLA, e.g., P1 ack in 15 minutes and resolution targets.
[10:31] Marcus (Redwood): for enterprise we can accept P1 ack in 15 minutes and a rolling update cadence; exact remediation windows depend on severity. we'll point you to our incident runbook.
[10:43] [11:00] Jules (Meridian): we also need to understand ephemeral key rotation and secrets management for long-lived sessions.
[11:08] Priya (Redwood): we support automatic key rotation; for BYOK we defer to your KMS rotation windows, Redwood will refresh wrapped keys without exposing plaintext. for sessions we recommend short-lived tokens and mTLS between services.
[11:24] [11:30] Sara (Meridian): are there any regulatory flags for payments companies? PCI scope concerns?
[11:36] Tom (Meridian): i can add — our PCI team will do a quick scoping call, but given we plan to restrict PII and use BYOK, scope should be limited.
[11:45] Alex (Redwood): we can provision a segregated environment for you if needed; that will affect pricing and provisioning lead time.
[11:54] [12:00] Karen (Meridian): legal will want explicit liability caps for the pilot period and clarity on data breach notification timelines.
[12:09] Alex (Redwood): that's fair — we'll propose pilot-specific liability caps in the SOW and standard breach notification windows in the DPA.
[12:18] [12:40] Priya (Redwood): technical follow-up: i'll need sample payloads and an API key for perf tests; can someone share a sanitized payload and a short-lived key?
[12:47] Jules (Meridian): we'll share sanitized payloads; procurement will issue a test account.
[12:52] Alex (Redwood): for the test account we'll generate a staging key with restricted perms.
[12:58] [13:30] Sara (Meridian): procurement will also need bank details or vendor code to draft the PO, who is our billing contact?
[13:37] Marcus (Redwood): billing contact is finance@redwood.ai and i'll include our vendor code in the packet.
[13:44] Alex (Redwood): ok next let's discuss the pilot acceptance criteria — what metrics does meridian want to use to call the pilot successful?
[13:55] Sara (Meridian): acceptance criteria: 1) functional parity for the top-10 intents, 2) p95 latency under 250ms for chat payloads, 3) less than 1% error rate, 4) security signoff on keying and logging.
[14:12] Alex (Redwood): sounds good. we'll map out tests for each.
[14:17] [14:40] Priya (Redwood): also recommend sanity evals for generation quality — we'll work with your product team to curate 50 prompts for regressions.
[14:26] Jules (Meridian): product will own that, we'll share the list.
[14:31] [15:00] Karen (Meridian): on insurance and indemnity — do you carry cyber insurance? what's the limit?
[15:08] Alex (Redwood): yes we carry cyber liability; i'll include policy summary in the security packet. current limit is stated in the docs.
[15:16] [15:30] Sara (Meridian): back to pricing — if the pilot goes well and we expand to dedicated capacity, what is the lead time for capacity provisioning?
[15:38] Priya (Redwood): standard lead time for dedicated pools is two to four weeks depending on GPU availability and region. we can offer burst capacity to bridge the gap for initial traffic.
[15:50] Alex (Redwood): note that dedicated capacity is a reserved commitment — procurement and finance will need the price and term to sign.
[15:59] [16:15] Jules (Meridian): can the pilot include simulated peak loads? we want to ensure your autoscaling and burst policies don't cause throttling surprises.
[16:24] Priya (Redwood): yes we'll include load tests up to your target concurrency and a separate run for failover scenarios.
[16:33] [16:50] Tom (Meridian): about the fall-back policy: if a region is degraded, will traffic automatically failover to another region and does that violate data residency?
[16:58] Marcus (Redwood): by default we won't failover across restricted residency boundaries unless you opt in; failover can be configured to keep data in-region or to route to a vetted fallback region. we'll document options.
[17:12] [17:30] Sara (Meridian): procurement will need a simplified legal packet — can you provide redline comments inline so legal can quickly see changes?
[17:38] Alex (Redwood): yes we will send an annotated redline and a summary for each major clause.
[17:44] [18:00] Karen (Meridian): about the dpa, we might need a clause for data subject access requests handling.
[18:07] Alex (Redwood): agreed — we'll propose standard DSR handling timelines and contact points.
[18:13] Priya (Redwood): one operational ask — do you want audit logs exported into your SIEM? we can push to your splunk or other syslog endpoints.
[18:24] Tom (Meridian): yes we want syslog to be available. we'll share endpoint details once infosec signs off.
[18:32] [19:00] Jules (Meridian): to summarize the technical ask list — sample payloads, concurrency targets, residency constraints, and rollback procedures. we'll send that as a doc.
[19:12] Alex (Redwood): great. we'll map those to runbook actions.
[19:20] [20:00] Marcus (Redwood): admin — i'll put together the SOW template and rate card; alex will do the legal redlines. priya will run the perf tests.
[20:11] Sara (Meridian): who will be our day-to-day contact?
[20:15] Alex (Redwood): alex for procurement/legal, priya for technical runbook, and marcus for billing and SOW.
[20:23] [21:00] Jules (Meridian): small nit — can you confirm if session data is encrypted at rest and in transit?
[21:08] Marcus (Redwood): yes in transit is TLS 1.2+ (we recommend 1.3), at rest we encrypt with AES-256 and keys are in KMS; we'll include specifics in the security packet.
[21:22] [22:00] Sara (Meridian): procurement: we'll probably route purchase through our standard three-way approval; we need to find a vendor code and invoice sample.
[22:10] Marcus (Redwood): will include invoice template.
[22:16] [23:00] Karen (Meridian): quick question on export controls — do you have any export-restricted model components?
[23:07] Alex (Redwood): we screen models for export controls and will flag any concerns; for typical open models there are no restrictions, but we will validate.
[23:20] [24:00] Priya (Redwood): perf note: we'll run two benchmarks — chat flows and long-document flows — and return p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1000 tokens.
[24:12] Jules (Meridian): okay.
[24:20] [25:00] Sara (Meridian): procurement wants a simple cancellation policy for the pilot; 30-day notice sounds ok but we want a pro-rated refund if you pre-billed.
[25:09] Alex (Redwood): we'll show pilot billing terms including pro-ration for pre-paid credit.
[25:18] [26:00] Marcus (Redwood): action owners recap: alex legal packet + redlines by sept 22; priya perf reports by sept 25; marcus billing invoice + vendor code by sept 22; meridian to send sanitized payloads and procurement checklist by sept 20.
[26:30] Sara (Meridian): yes we'll share the checklist and payloads.
[26:36] [27:00] Karen (Meridian): on indemnity, we'll take a look at your proposed carve-outs and escalate if needed.
[27:10] Alex (Redwood): understood.
[27:16] [28:00] Jules (Meridian): one last technical: do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs for parsing? we have a downstream parser that expects JSON.
[28:27] Priya (Redwood): yes we support structured outputs and function-like tool calling. we'll send sample payloads for structured responses too.
[28:40] [29:00] Tom (Meridian): security follow-up: will you allow us to run an appsec or pen test during the pilot?
[29:07] Marcus (Redwood): yes we support tenant-scoped pen tests; we'll coordinate a safe window and a scope doc.
[29:18] [30:00] Sara (Meridian): great. any other blockers?
[30:05] Karen (Meridian): legal wants to confirm the process for data deletion requests in the event of contract end.
[30:12] Alex (Redwood): we'll add a deletion appendix with timelines and proof of deletion.
[30:20] [31:00] Priya (Redwood): can we get access to your staging endpoint traffic shape? that helps with batching config.
[31:09] Jules (Meridian): yes we'll provide request distribution charts.
[31:15] [32:00] Alex (Redwood): ok wrapping: we'll produce the packet by sept 22. recap next steps and owners in follow-up email.
[32:12] Sara (Meridian): thank you.
[32:16] [33:00] Marcus (Redwood): small note — competitors were mentioned, you had evaluated openai and anthropic; any specific price or capability gaps?
[33:10] Sara (Meridian): openai price was competitive but we worried about data residency and enterprise SLAs; anthropic had better safety primitives but higher cost.
[33:26] Alex (Redwood): understood.
[33:30] [34:00] Priya (Redwood): i'll include model variant recommendations that balance cost and quality.
[34:08] [35:00] Jules (Meridian): procurement note — we may ask for a 60-day net payment term. is that acceptable?
[35:08] Marcus (Redwood): billing usually standard net-30, but for larger enterprise we can negotiate net-45/60 with approvals. we'll surface that in the SOW.
[35:22] [36:00] Sara (Meridian): ok i'll flag that with finance.
[36:05] Karen (Meridian): legal will review once we get your redlines.
[36:10] [37:00] Alex (Redwood): thanks everyone. final check — any regulatory constraints or special compliance we missed?
[37:10] Tom (Meridian): none beyond pci/data residency.
[37:14] Alex (Redwood): perfect. we will send the package and schedule the technical runbook.
[37:20] [38:00] Priya (Redwood): i'll follow with perf tests once we get payloads and staging creds.
[38:08] Jules (Meridian): we'll get those over by sept 20.
[38:12] [39:00] Alex (Redwood): i'll follow with redlines and the SOW.
[39:07] Sara (Meridian): thanks.
[39:10] [40:00] (crosstalk) multiple: thanks bye.
[40:12] End meeting.

Notes about transcription: occasional recognition errors present; proper nouns may be slightly off (e.g., "msadpa" typed together). The recording duration is ~48 minutes but the auto-summary captured key items above.
